pair_scope.research_question: Do two independent first-party human-plasma polystyrene protein-corona studies expose reusable unit-level numeric size maps and a harmonizable quantitative protein endpoint?
pair_scope.primary_search_method: Primary article pages and their stated supplementary-data availability were screened; no bulk asset was downloaded.
pair_scope.candidate_selection_rule: Distinct publication laboratories with human-plasma protein-corona proteomics, explicit 50/100 nm polystyrene size design and quantitative protein endpoint.

candidates.publication_title: Nanoparticle size and surface properties determine the protein corona with possible implications for biological impacts
non_admission_reasons: The primary article reports the 50/100 nm size design, but the source-file/result-unit byte map has not been downloaded and checksum-verified.
The named supplementary XLS is not yet audited for reuse terms and cannot be placed in the public CC0 cohort by article citation alone.
The hard-corona identification workflow is not yet shown to share a preprocessing and endpoint scale with the PNNL study.

candidates.publication_title: Quantitative proteomics analysis of adsorbed plasma proteins classifies nanoparticles with different surface properties and size
non_admission_reasons: The primary article reports 24 size/surface/time conditions and quantitative protein abundance, but the source result bytes and unit-level size join have not been checksum-verified.
The article is not evidence of a CC0 redistribution licence for every supplementary asset.
The AMT/18O quantitative scale and on-particle digestion workflow cannot be concatenated with the UCD hard-corona output before a shared endpoint contract is frozen.
